If $\dfrac{d}{dx}x\ln x=\ln x+1$ then

$$\int_e^{2e}\dfrac{d}{dx}x\ln x\,dx=\int_e^{2e}\ln x\,dx+\int_e^{2e}1\,dx$$

$$\big[x\ln x\big]_e^{2e}=\int_e^{2e}\ln x\,dx+\big[x\big]_e^{2e}$$

$$\therefore\int_e^{2e}\ln x\,dx=\big[x\ln x\big]_e^{2e}-\big[x\big]_e^{2e}=2e\ln 2e-e\ln e-(2e-e)$$

$$=2e\ln 2e-e\ln e-e$$

$$=2e\ln 2e-e-e=2e\ln 2e-2e=2e(\ln 2+\ln e)-2e=2e\ln 2$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: Marker note: the line $2e\ln 2e-e\ln e-e$ is sufficient.

solutions.latex:
$f'(x)=12x-6x^2=6x(2-x)$

Since $(2,8)$ is the maximum, $6x=0\Rightarrow x=0$, $y=0$ is the minimum turning point.

$f''(x)=12-12x$

Possible inflexion at $f''(x)=0$: $0=12-12x$, so $x=1$.

Since $x=1$ is between the maximum turning point $(2,8)$ and the minimum turning point $(0,0)$, $(1,4)$ is an inflexion point.

OR

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 0 & 1 & 2\\ \hline f''(x) & 12 & 0 & -12 \end{array}$$

Concave up then concave down: concavity changes, so $(1,4)$ is an inflexion point.

Venn diagram: Facebook only $23\%$, both $22\%$, Instagram only $11\%$, neither $44\%$.

$P(\text{Fb}\cap\text{Insta})=22\%$

$f(x)=\dfrac{8}{3}x-\dfrac{4}{3}x^3$

$f'(x)=\dfrac{8}{3}-4x^2$

Mode is a maximum turning point, so $f'(x)=0$:

$0=\dfrac{8}{3}-4x^2$

$4x^2=\dfrac{8}{3}$

$x^2=\dfrac{2}{3}$

$x=\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$ but $0<x<1$

$\therefore x=\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$, a maximum as $f'(x)$ is an upside-down parabola.

$\therefore x=\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$ is the mode $\approx 0.82$ (2 d.p.)

$\dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{4}(3x^2-10x-8)$

Maximum when $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$:

$0=3x^2-10x-8=(3x+2)(x-4)$

$x=-\dfrac{2}{3}$ or $x=4$

But as $(4-x)^2$ is a length, $4-x>0$, so $x<4$. $\therefore x=-\dfrac{2}{3}$.

Test: $$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & -1 & -\frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3}\\ \hline \frac{dA}{dx} & \frac{5}{4} & 0 & -\frac{13}{12} \end{array}$$

$\therefore$ maximum at $x=-\dfrac{2}{3}$.

$PQ=-\dfrac{2}{3}+3=\dfrac{7}{3}$, $PR=\left(4-\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\right)^2=\dfrac{196}{9}$

$$QR^2=\left(\dfrac{7}{3}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{196}{9}\right)^2-2\times\dfrac{7}{3}\times\dfrac{196}{9}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}$$

$$=\dfrac{38857}{81}-\dfrac{2744}{27}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=391.70\ldots$$

$QR=19.79\ldots\approx 19.8$ (1 d.p.)
